questions.question: When using ABS brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake pedal harder than normal.
Press the brake pedal the same way you normally would.
Press the brake pedal more lightly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal the same way you normally would.
questions.explanation: Use ABS brakes the same way you use regular brakes. Do not change how hard or soft you press the pedal.

questions.question: How does centering cargo on a truck help?

options.text: It lets you drive faster.
It prevents the truck from rolling over.
It makes turns more dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents the truck from rolling over.
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loads make rollovers more likely. Keep cargo centered on the truck to prevent dangerous rollovers.

questions.question: Why should you back a trailer toward the driver's side?

options.text: You can see the back of the vehicle better.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the back of the vehicle better.
questions.explanation: Back toward the left side of the vehicle. This gives you the best view of the rear.

questions.question: What should you do when driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Use only the air brakes.
Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On steep hills, use engine braking in a low gear to control your speed. Use the brakes only when needed to help.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It reduces the vehicle's braking power.
It works with other braking systems and does not reduce braking power.
It does not work on large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It works with other braking systems and does not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with your regular brakes and does not change how much braking power you have. It only activates when the wheels are about to lock.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?

options.text: Water and oil
Ammonia
Liquid cleaners

questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If these build up, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What happens if you stay in neutral too long while shifting gears?

options.text: The vehicle will speed up.
You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
You may stall the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long, the next gear may be hard to engage. Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up the engine to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: When pulling two semi-trailers, where should you place the lighter one?

options.text: At the very end of the combination.
At the very end right after the tractor.
Any trailer can go in any position.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the very end of the combination.
questions.explanation: Put the heavier trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lighter trailer at the end.

questions.question: Is eating while driving safe?

options.text: Yes, it saves time.
No, it is dangerous.
Yes, if the food is easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is dangerous.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, and smoking distract you from driving. Plan stops to eat during long trips.

questions.question: What should you do if your engine catches fire?

options.text: Open the hood right away.
Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turning off the engine stops the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless you must.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake.
Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it can damage the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is below freezing.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
Stop air from entering the air brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To uncouple the trailers.
To test the trailer brakes.
To apply the emergency brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: To test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Using the trailer hand valve while driving can cause a skid. Use it only when testing the trailer brakes.

questions.question: What happens when traveling downhill?

options.text: Your vehicle slows down.
Your vehicle travels at the same speed as on level ground.
Your vehicle speeds up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle speeds up.
questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to go faster when going downhill. Reduce your speed before you reach a downhill section.

questions.question: What do drivers often do when stuck behind a slow vehicle?

options.text: Follow too closely.
Give the vehicle plenty of space.
Are happy with the speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Drivers often tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?

options.text: Once a week.
Once a month.
After every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your vehicle at the end of each trip, day, or shift. Complete a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact to communicate with them.
Ignore their gestures.
Do not move out of their way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their gestures.
questions.explanation: Get out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as this can upset them. Do not let them provoke you.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what is true about air tanks?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, what should you check about the belt?

options.text: That it is thin.
That it is properly tightened.
That it is cracked.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is properly tightened.
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: How does an empty truck compare to a full truck in terms of stopping distance?

options.text: An empty truck stops in a shorter distance.
An empty truck stops in a longer distance.
Both trucks stop in the same distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: An empty truck stops in a longer distance.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need a longer distance to stop because they have less traction.
